# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual specifies a definite wire order, but Deaf can only receive gestures. I will encode the words “PURPLE BLUE RED” in Morse using a circular hand as dot, a horizontal pointing hand as dash, claps as letter separators, and raised hands as word separators. This gives Deaf a visually recognizable, self-contained encoding of the required sequence.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","👉","👉","👌","👏","👌","👌","👉","👏","👌","👉","👌","👏","👌","👉","👉","👌","👏","👌","👉","👌","👌","👏","👌","🙌","👉","👌","👌","👌","👏","👌","👉","👌","👌","👏","👌","👌","👉","👏","👌","🙌","👌","👉","👌","👏","👌","👏","👉","👌","👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report: keypad positions 1 through 4 are engraved digits 1, 5, 2, 8 respectively; no digits entered. Strip has three engraved marks: first and third are the same unpronounceable glyph, while the middle is a different unpronounceable glyph. I cannot feel display, light, or wire identities.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb: display 9; light red; strip green yellow yellow; keypad positions 1=1, 2=5, 3=2, 4=8, nothing entered; wires in order: yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. I cannot decode your gesture sequence. Please gesture a code legend or an unambiguous instruction for Blind.

Blind’s tactile report confirms the physical positions, while Deaf can see the wire order. The manual’s required colors correspond to wire positions 5 (purple), 3 (blue), and 4 (red). Since Deaf could not decode my earlier encoding, I will send those positions directly as easily countable hand-number gestures, separated by claps: five, three, four. Deaf can relay “cut positions 5, then 3, then 4” to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐","👏","🤟","👏","🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can physically press keypad slots 1-4 or cut wire positions 1-6, and nothing else. Deaf reports display 9; red light; strip colors green-yellow-yellow; keypad positions 1-5-2-8; wires positions 1-6 yellow-white-blue-red-purple-green. Please use the manual to determine a safe action and tell me directly by spoken position/action.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is now 3 and light yellow; all other visible details unchanged. Your gestures have no agreed meaning to me. Use this relay code: 👌=0, 👉=1; send each letter as exactly five binary gestures using A=00001 through Z=11010; put 👏 between letters and 🙌 between words. I will decode and speak the manual instruction to Blind. Please resend the required action in that code.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports the visible state changed without action: display is now 3 and light is now yellow. Strip and physical controls remain as previously reported. I am waiting for your explicit safe instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: Current view: display 2, light red; strip green-yellow-yellow; wires yellow white blue red purple green. I decoded your code as CUT WIRE F HEN THEE COURE, which is ambiguous. Please resend the exact complete action slowly in our five-bit code, checking each five-symbol letter. State the wire by its color name and any required follow-up action.

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says do not act: your decoded instruction is corrupted or ambiguous. Current visual state reported: display 2, red light, strip green-yellow-yellow, wires yellow-white-blue-red-purple-green. Please send only an explicit unambiguous action to me when certain.
Deaf says to Mute: Decoded clearly: CUT PURPLE THEN BLUE THEN RED. I have relayed it to Blind.

Deaf has now decoded the manual instruction correctly and says it has been relayed to Blind. Since I cannot communicate directly with Blind and no further instruction is required by the manual, I will wait for Blind to receive and act on that relay.

```text
wait()
```
